```{r functions, echo=FALSE}
draw_half_court <- function() {
  court_theme <- theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.title = element_blank(),
      axis.text = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks = element_blank(),
      panel.grid = element_blank()
    )
  
  court <- ggplot() +
    # Court elements
    geom_circle(aes(x0 = 0, y0 = 0, r = 7.5), color = "gray") +   # Rim area
    geom_rect(aes(xmin = -8, xmax = 8, ymin = 0, ymax = 19), fill = NA, color = "gray") + # Paint
    geom_rect(aes(xmin = -25, xmax = 25, ymin = -5, ymax = 47), fill = NA, color = "black") + # Court border
    geom_circle(aes(x0 = 0, y0 = 19, r = 6), color = "gray") + # Free throw
    geom_segment(aes(x = -22, y = 0, xend = -22, yend = 14), color = "gray") + # 3pt line
    geom_segment(aes(x = 22, y = 0, xend = 22, yend = 14), color = "gray") +
    geom_curve(aes(x = -22, y = 14, xend = 22, yend = 14),
               curvature = -1, color = "gray") +
    coord_fixed() +
    court_theme
  return(court)
}

draw_half_court_layers <- function() {
  list(
    geom_circle(aes(x0 = 0, y0 = 0, r = 7.5), inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "gray"),   # Rim
    geom_rect(aes(xmin = -8, xmax = 8, ymin = 0, ymax = 19), inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = NA, color = "gray"),  # Paint
    geom_rect(aes(xmin = -25, xmax = 25, ymin = -5, ymax = 47), inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = NA, color = "black"),  # Border
    geom_circle(aes(x0 = 0, y0 = 19, r = 6), inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "gray"),  # Free throw
    geom_segment(aes(x = -22, y = 0, xend = -22, yend = 14), inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "gray"),  # 3pt sides
    geom_segment(aes(x = 22, y = 0, xend = 22, yend = 14), inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "gray"),
    geom_curve(aes(x = -22, y = 14, xend = 22, yend = 14), inherit.aes = FALSE, curvature = -1, color = "gray"),  # 3pt arc
    coord_fixed(),
    theme_minimal() +
      theme(
        axis.title = element_blank(),
        axis.text = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank()
      )
  )
}
```

The NBA Cup is a recent addition to regular season play with a tournament debut in 2023. All NBA Cup games contribute to regular season records except the championship game.

The Bucks' 2024 NBA Cup championship game was played against a team who, in regular season, had the highest offensive and defensive rating in the NBA (compared to our no.11). OKC is a statistically sound team with superstars and MVP nominees like Shai Gilgeous-Alexander accompanied by a deep roster of heavy contributors. During there first match-up of the year, without doubt, the OKC Thunder were expected to walk away with this trophy. What circumstances fostered the Bucks' success in the NBA Cup finals?

```{r import data, include=FALSE}
shots <- read_csv("data_mil_okc_121724_shots(in).csv")
team_min <- read_csv("NBA_Cup_Minutes_Played - Sheet1.csv")

str(shots)
str(team_min)
```

### League-Wide Norms

```{r, echo=FALSE}
ggplot(shots, aes(x = contestLevel, y = qSQ)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, height = 0) +
  geom_smooth(aes(group = 1), method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Scatterplot of qSQ vs Defensive Contest",
       x = "Contest Level",
       y = "Quality Shot (qSQ)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r regression, echo=FALSE}
# Fit the regression model
nba_contest_model <- lm(qSQ ~ contestLevel, data = shots) 
pander(nba_contest_model)
```

The regression reveals a highly significant negative relationship between variables; that across teams, as contest level goes up (i.e uncontested to heavily contested), the probability that a shot goes in goes down. These results are expected since tougher defenses across the NBA will produce lower scoring opportunities for opponents.

## Team-Level Analyses

#### Shot Quality vs. Shot Success

```{r shotsuccess, echo=FALSE}
#include 3 pt attempts
sqvss <-shots %>%
  group_by(team_nba_off) %>%
  summarise(avg_qSQ = mean(qSQ, na.rm = TRUE),
            actual_fg_pct = sum(fg)/sum(fga)) %>%
  arrange(desc(avg_qSQ)) 

kable(sqvss, col.names = c("Team", "Avg Shot Make Probability", "Actual FG Pct"))
```

However, reference table XXXX reveals that Though we had nearly identical shot quality, the gap in actual field goal percentage could point to exceptional Bucks defense or cold shooting from OKC.

one of two stories - we forced them into making tough shots and shots fell for us the other story is that

#### Defensive Contest

```{r, echo=FALSE}
dc <- shots %>%
  group_by(contestLevel, team_nba_off) %>%
  summarise(fg_pct = sum(fg)/sum(fga),
            avg_qSQ = mean(qSQ, na.rm = TRUE),
            attempts = n()) %>%
  arrange(fg_pct)
kable(dc, col.names = c("Contest Level", "Team", "FG Pct", "Avg Shot Make Prob", "Attempts"))
```

##### Uncontested

OKC took slightly more difficult uncontested shots and were more efficient from them, meaning our defense likely slacked off due to the perceived low probability that a shot would go in.

##### Lightly Contested

Avg shot `qSQ` difficulty was comparable however, we converted at a much higher rate! Our ability to convert lightly contested shots at a higher rate could indicate superior shot selection and offensive execution.

OKC's low conversion on lightly contested shots point to a Bucks defense forcing OKC into shooting tougher shots. This is confirmed in scoring and shooting performance by player table \*\*

##### Heavily Contested

The average shot difficulty `qSQ` was similar for both teams, OKC was able to achieve slightly better shooting performance in the presence of heavy defense. This points to a high defensive caliber of both teams; us matching the tenacity of OKC, the NBA's regular season leader in defensive rating, with our own resilient defense.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
defense_summary <- shots %>%
  group_by(team_nba_def) %>%
  summarize(
    opponent_fg_pct = mean(sum(fg)/sum(fga)),  # Averaging FGs when this team is defending
    avg_qSQ_against = mean(qSQ, na.rm = TRUE), # Average shot quality faced by this team's defense
    avg_contest_level = mean(as.numeric(factor(contestLevel)), na.rm = TRUE), # If contest level is ordered
    attempts_faced = n(),    # Total attempts faced by the defense
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# Use kable to display the defense summary table
kable(defense_summary, digits = 3, caption = "Defense Performance Summary by Team")
```

We held OKC to a much lower field goal percentage on many more attempts.

#### Catch-and-shoot Effectiveness

```{r, echo=FALSE}
cse <- shots %>%
  filter(catchAndShoot == 1) %>% 
  group_by(team_nba_off) %>%
  summarise(fg_pct = sum(fg)/sum(fga),
            avg_qSQ = mean(qSQ, na.rm = TRUE),
            attempts = n())
kable(cse)
```

The similarity in average shot quality (MIL: 55.2, OKC: 55.4) indicates that both teams were generating similar quality of catch-and-shoot opportunities. This suggests that this disparity in FG% is not due to the types of shots taken, but rather the effectiveness of their execution and exceptional Bucks defense.

The higher attempt rate also signifies MIL's ability to create more opportunities through effective ball movement and off-ball player movement. The game strategy focused on leveraging catch-and-shoot opportunities contributed to greater scoring.

#### Court Region and Shot Type

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# crst <- shots%>%

# kable(crst)
crst <- shots %>%
  group_by(team_nba_off, region) %>%
  summarise(
    fg_pct = sum(fg)/sum(fga),
    attempts = n(),
    .groups = 'drop'  # Drop grouping to avoid implicit grouping layers
  ) %>%
  filter(fg_pct > 0) %>%  # Filter out rows where fg_pct is zero
  arrange(desc(fg_pct))

# Display the filtered results as a table
kable(crst)
```

We were extremely effective from high-value zones, (e.i., Left wing three, Right corner three ,Restricted area (RA)

In contrast, OKC underperformed in their strongholds:RA: 40%, Key: 45.8%, Middle two: 50% on just 6 shots

This means we didn't just shoot better, we shot better from smarter, higher value areas.

Heat Map

```{r heat map, echo=FALSE}
shots %>%
  filter(team_nba_off %in% c("MIL", "OKC")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = loc_x, y = loc_y)) +
  geom_density_2d_filled(alpha = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~team_nba_off) +
  draw_half_court_layers() +
  labs(title = "Shot Density: Bucks vs. OKC") +
  theme_minimal()
```

From the heat map and bar chart, we can draw that OKC had greater diversity in their shot selection; many more types of shots fell for them. However, we had noticeably higher catch and shoot makes and catch and shoot makes with a relocation, indicating that OKC has trouble defending a player when moving to a different spot to shoot from.

#### Scoring and shooting performance by team

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Group by team and player, then calculate the metrics
shooting_data <- shots %>%
  group_by(team_nba_off, player_nba_shooter) %>%
  summarize(
    FGA = sum(fga),
    FG = sum(fg),
    FG_Percentage = mean(sum(fg)/sum(fga)),
    ThreePA = sum(fga3),
    ThreeP = sum(fg3),
    ThreeP_Percentage = mean(sum(fg3) / sum(fga3), na.rm = TRUE),
    Avg_Distance = mean(distance, na.rm = TRUE),
    Avg_qSQ = mean(qSQ, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  arrange(team_nba_off, desc(Avg_qSQ))

# Display the results
kable(shooting_data)
```

##### Bucks

Starters like Dame, Giannis and Brook maintained high `FG` and `ThreeP` percentages while steadily creating shots with low difficulty/ higher make probabilities.

Forwards like [Taurean Prince]{.underline} creating shots with **higher make probabilities** and guards like Green and Trent Jr. shooting maintaining outstanding `ThreeP` efficientcies while creating shots with higher probabilities of makes, compared to starters like Dame, undoubtedly contributed to the team's success.

This table outlines a successful game plan that aligned with player's strengths and set them up for success.

##### OKC

Starters like Shai took a larger number of improbable shots thus converting on only a third of his `FG` and an even lower percentage of `ThreeP`. Other starters with `qSQ` averages in the low 50's shot

#### Assists and Passing by team

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Group by team and player, then calculate the metrics
assist_data <- shots %>%
  group_by(team_nba_off) %>%
  summarize(
    Assist_Opps = sum(assistOpp),
    Assisted_Shots = sum(assisted),
    Assist_Avg = Assist_Opps/Assisted_Shots
  ) %>%
  arrange(team_nba_off, desc(Assist_Opps))

# Display the results
kable(assist_data)
```

#### Shot Quality vs. Makes for starters and bench

```{r, echo=FALSE}
#merging
team_min$MIN <- as.numeric(team_min$MIN, units = "mins")
team_min <- team_min %>%
  mutate(MIN = as.numeric(MIN) / 60)
team_min <- team_min %>%
  mutate(MIN = as.numeric(MIN) / 60)

# Merge datasets and calculate efficiency metrics
combined_data <- shots %>%
  left_join(select(team_min, Player, Team, MIN, STATUS), by = c("player_nba_shooter" = "Player", "team_nba_off" = "Team")) %>%
  group_by(player_nba_shooter, team_nba_off, STATUS) %>%
  summarize(
    Total_Points = sum(sum(fg)*2,sum(fg3)*3),  # Assuming 'fg' captures points from made shots. You might need actual points if available.
    Attempts = sum(fga),
    Minutes_Played = first(MIN),  # Picking minutes from `team_min`
    PPM = Total_Points / Minutes_Played,  # Points per minute
    FG_Percentage = Total_Points / Attempts
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  arrange(team_nba_off, desc(PPM))

# Display the summarized results
knitr::kable(combined_data)

# Visualization: Minutes Played vs Points per Minute
ggplot(combined_data, aes(x = Minutes_Played, y = PPM, color = STATUS)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(method = 'lm', se = FALSE, color = 'gray') +
  facet_wrap(~ team_nba_off) +
  labs(
    title = "Relationship between Minutes Played and Points per Minute",
    x = "Minutes Played",
    y = "Points per Minute"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Visualization: Minutes Played vs Field Goal Percentage
ggplot(combined_data, aes(x = Minutes_Played, y = FG_Percentage, color = STATUS)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(method = 'lm', se = FALSE, color = 'gray') +
  facet_wrap(~ team_nba_off) +
  labs(
    title = "Minutes Played vs Field Goal Percentage",
    x = "Minutes Played",
    y = "Field Goal Percentage"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Conclusions

We seemed to have optimized our help-defense and closeout structure: Maintaining high contest frequency without sacrificing defensive integrity. This implies a high-IQ rotation scheme and strong communication.
